title.value: LayerDecompose: Exploring weight sharing for Large Language Model Compression

abstract.value: Recent advances in large language model (LLM) compression have predominantly focused on pruning and low-rank factorization, leaving weight sharing—despite its success in classical neural network compression—largely unexplored. We introduce LayerDecompose, a novel framework that reduces parameter redundancy by sharing a core weight matrix across transformer layers and augmenting each layer with lightweight, low-rank adapters. Unlike prior SVD- and pruning-based methods, our joint optimization of shared weights and residual adapters achieves a 30% model size reduction while retaining 89% of the original performance on seven standard benchmarks. Experiments on LLaMA and other models demonstrate that LayerDecompose consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines. These results highlight the promise of combining weight sharing with low-rank adaptation for efficient, scalable LLM deployment.

primary_area.value: foundation or frontier models, including LLMs
